html:
SMTO-EML-0026 — This email sender's sign-in setup has the wrong kind of entry

GUID: 270286e3-bb6a-574d-b070-df0041c478f4
Slug: email-auth-configuration-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The saved sign-in entries this sender points to exist, but one is the wrong kind of entry or has settings SMTO can't accept. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store, select the sender, open Value, select Reveal & edit value, and note the name in auth_ref. That name must point to a sign-in connection entry, not to some other kind of entry.
  2. Open the entry with that name and check that its profile_type is oauth2_connection and its client_ref names an entry whose profile_type is oauth2_client. If the sender points at the app entry instead of the connection entry, or the connection points at the wrong app entry, SMTO stops here.
  3. Correct the wrong name or setting, or recreate the entry from the matching Email OAuth Connection or Email OAuth App template, then select Save. SMTO checks each sign-in entry's kind and settings before it will use them.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to connect the email account, then to test the connection. This confirms the corrected entries work together.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the sender's sign-in status, such as ready or authorization required, instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who set up email sign-in for SMTO. Don't change your email password; this is a setup problem in SMTO, not a rejected password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A referenced OAuth profile has the wrong profile_type (the connection must be oauth2_connection and its client oauth2_client) or fails auth profile validation.

What this means

  • A referenced OAuth profile has an incompatible type or invalid configuration. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • A referenced OAuth profile has the wrong type or fails configuration validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the records at auth.auth_ref and at that connection's client_ref in Parameter Store; ensure profile_type is oauth2_connection and oauth2_client respectively and that both pass agent_runtime.auth.profiles.validate. Correct them, then run email.connect and email.connection_status before testing SMTP authorization.
  • Correct the referenced OAuth connection or client profile and validate its type before testing authorization.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • The referenced connection and client meet their profile contracts.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
